The hottest AI wearables hackathon of the year is almost here. 🔥

$15,000+ in prizes. A YC final interview for the winning team. One day to build something people haven’t seen before.

On November 14, we’re bringing VexoHacks to @ycombinator in San Francisco for a full day of building with AI wearables, voice and vision.

Bring your ideas. We’ll have Vexo bracelets ready for teams who want to build with our voice tech.

Huge thanks to @openai , @googledeepmind , @elevenlabs , Stripe, @brexhq ,Mastra @minimax_ai.official and Superserve for making it happen.

Limited capacity. Entry by application only. Apply before it’s too late.

👉 https://events.ycombinator.com/vexohacks

#AI #Wearables #VexoHacks

My name is Farqaleet, but most people call me Kiani. I’ve always loved building things. 

As a kid I took things apart and found ways to put them back together. So in university i pursued a degree in mechatronics engineering. I’ve worked at AMD, General Motors and was a Senior Software Engineer at Tesla. 

Over the years I had the privilege to mentor many bright young minds. One day my mentee ( Haris ) told me about an idea he had with his friend Vikram, he wanted to build the future of AI Wearables, and he wanted me to help lead the hardware. 

I had originally hired Haris for this drive and energy, and he would always pitch me startup ideas. I was intrigued because I love hardware and found the AI Wearable space very interesting. It was a tough decision, could I really leave a stable job at Tesla to work at a startup? But I thought about it, and if there’s anyone who could disrupt this space, it’s Haris. 

I believed in the vision from that moment on, and I packed my bags and moved to San Francisco to start VEXO. Now we’re gearing up for Demo Day at Y Combinator.
